markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The only plausible shifts before 2027 would require an abrupt health crisis or an unprecedented internal challenge capable of upending the current power structure.

This market will resolve to the person who wins the 2028 US Presidential Election. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

eventMetadata.context_description: JD Vance holds the top position in the 2028 winner market at 25.4% amid a fragmented field, reflecting his status as sitting vice president to a term-limited president and positioning as the continuity candidate within the Republican coalition. The 2028 US Presidential Election is scheduled to take place on November 7, 2028.

This market will resolve to the person who wins the 2028 US Presidential Election. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

eventMetadata.context_description: JD Vance holds the top position in the 2028 winner market at 25.4% amid a fragmented field, reflecting his status as sitting vice president to a term-limited president and positioning as the continuity candidate within the Republican coalition. Marco Rubio follows at 10.3% as another administration figure, while Democratic contenders remain dispersed, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 12.0% and Jon Ossoff at 11.5% drawing support from distinct party factions. Traders price the wide-open contest this way because early primary positioning, fundraising signals, and polling among likely voters show no dominant nominee on either side ahead of the 2026 midterms and formal 2028 announcements. Key differentiators include incumbency advantages for Republicans versus coalition-building requirements for Democrats, with consolidation likely hinging on midterm results, primary calendar dynamics, and candidate endorsements that narrow viable paths to nomination.
